newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cyclone floods NE Australia, cotton spared.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cyclone floods NE Australia, cotton spared.

text.p: Cyclone Justin, which crossed the Queensland coast on the weekend just north of Cairns, had moved south to just southeast of Townsville at 11.40 a.m. (0040 GMT) on Monday, the Bureau of Meteorology's Cyclone Warning Centre told Reuters.
The cyclone had been moving southeast at about 15 km an hour but in the last hour it had slowed right down, an official said.
"At the moment it's barely a cyclone," he said.
The present concern was that it might redevelop if it headed out to sea, as seemed likely if it continued to track south to Bowen, he said.
Flooding had been heavy in coastal rivers south of Cairns, he said.
Very heavy falls were recorded in the Townsville area over the weekend, with 200-300 millimetres recorded around that city and with a downpour of 465 mm recorded in one area nearby, he said.
Flood warnings were current for the Herbert, Tully, Haughton and Burdekin Rivers, where the heaviest rain had fallen in the past few days.
The Tully River had cut a highway while the Herbert River had produced major floods around Ingham.
But the heaviest rainfall was starting to ease and some rainfall heading south did not appear to be serious, he said.
Present indications were that Queensland's cotton crop, in the south of the state, was not affected by fallout from Justin, weather bureau and cotton industry officials said.
The sugar industry was badly affected, industry officials said, but the extent of the damage was still being determined.
Queensland accounts for about 95 percent of Australia's sugar crop.
